title: Why Your Vet Bill Is $2,000 Now (Who Bought Your Vet)
alts: Why Vet Bills Got So Expensive (It's Not Just Inflation)
Who Really Owns Your Vet Clinic Now?
line1: Dave's dog needed knee surgery. The bill: $2,000. Here's who bought up the vet industry, and why the price never shows up on a sign.
summary: Dave's dog Biscuit tears a knee ligament and needs surgery today. The bill shocks him: $2,000. We break down why: private equity and corporate roll-ups (Mars/VCA, JAB Holding) now own a big share of vet clinics, especially emergency ones, how a 'roll-up' actually works, why vet prices almost never get posted anywhere (unlike human hospitals), the emergency-hours markup, why vet prices have risen faster than almost anything else in the CPI basket since 2019, the fast-growing pet insurance industry (NAPHIA data), and how CareCredit payment plans work. Then, practical, pet-loving advice: get quotes, insure early, build a small emergency fund, and ask who owns your clinic.
